505　營運資金管理505　Working Capital Management

對齊中五選修財務管理 505（課堂筆記《營運資金管理》）。本章有：營業循環和現金轉換循環、現金管理三原則、現金預算和現金管理的關係、應收帳款與應付帳款政策、經濟訂貨量和再訂購水平。本章沒有：編製整份現金預算、把「2/10、n/30」自行換算成年率、風險管理（見 506）。資本投資的回收期和淨現值見 504。 Aligned with F5 Elective Financial Management 505 (class notes Working Capital Management). This chapter covers the operating cycle and cash conversion cycle, the principles of cash management, the link between the cash budget and cash management, accounts receivable and accounts payable policies, the economic order quantity and the re-order point. Preparing a full cash-budget worksheet, turning a quote such as 2/10, n/30 into an annual rate, and risk management are not in this chapter; see 506 for risk management. Payback and NPV are in 504.

讀完本章，應能：

After this chapter you should be able to:

1　營運資金管理Working capital management

1.1　介紹Introduction

營運資金管理指同時管理企業的流動資產和流動負債，讓企業有充足的短期變現能力，應付其日常營運。

Working capital management refers to the simultaneous management of current assets and current liabilities so as to provide sufficient short-term liquidity to support a firm’s daily operation.

營運資金管理Working capital management
↓
現金管理Cash management
應收帳款管理Accounts receivable management
應付帳款管理Accounts payable management
存貨管理Inventory management

1.2　營運資金管理的重要性The importance of working capital management

  • 營運資金管理有助企業維持變現能力，所以它對企業的成敗起關鍵作用。
  • Working capital management is essential for the survival of a firm.
  • 即使企業有高的盈利能力，如果它沒有足夠的現金去償還短期債務，它也是營運失敗。
  • Even though a business is profitable, it may fail if it cannot generate a sufficient amount of cash from operations to meet its short-term obligations.

有盈利，不等於過得了短期現金關。考試要的是變現能力，不是再寫一次盈利能力。

A profit does not mean the firm can meet this week’s cash needs. The point is liquidity, not another sentence about profitability.

請茶的星期五茶葉單Try Tea’s Friday tea bill

小明說：「屯門請茶這個月有盈利，所以星期五付不了茶葉商也沒有問題。」錯。盈利沒有變成足夠現金去償還這筆短期債務，店一樣可以營運失敗。

Bob says: “Try Tea in Tuen Mun made a profit this month, so it does not matter if they cannot pay the tea supplier on Friday.” He is wrong. A profit that has not become enough cash to meet that short-term obligation can still bring the shop down.

小練習 505.1Quick check 505.1

題 1Q1

小明的句子錯在哪裡？

Where is Bob’s sentence wrong?

答案：有盈利仍可能沒有足夠現金償還短期債務，營運一樣失敗

Answer: a profitable firm may still fail if it cannot raise enough cash for its short-term obligations

Textbook exercise: P. 174 Q2

1.3　營業循環和現金轉換循環Operating cycle and cash conversion cycle

營業循環Operating cycle

營業循環是由企業賒購存貨到售出產品收取現金的期間。

The operating cycle is the time period from when a firm buys its inventory on credit to when it receives a cash payment from selling its products.

營業循環 = 存貨階段 ＋ 收回應收帳款階段

Operating cycle = inventory period + receivables collection period

當營業循環愈短，資產便能愈快變現為現金，所以企業營運資金管理的效率愈高。

The shorter the operating cycle time, the faster the asset is converted into cash; thus, the more benefit for the finances of the company.

現金轉換循環Cash conversion cycle

現金轉換循環是由企業以現金支付購貨款項到售出產品收取現金的期間。

The cash conversion cycle is the time period from when a firm pays cash to buy inventory to when it receives cash back from the sale of products.

現金轉換循環 = 存貨階段 ＋ 收回應收帳款階段 － 支付應付帳款階段

Cash conversion cycle = inventory period + receivables collection period − payables repayment period

On the diagram this middle stretch is called the payable deferral period. In the formula it is the payables repayment period. They are the same period.

上面整段是營業循環。現金轉換循環由付現那一點才開始，所以比營業循環短一個支付應付帳款階段。The top span is the operating cycle. The cash conversion cycle starts only when cash is paid, so it is shorter by the payables period.

企業的其中一個目標是減短它的現金轉換循環，避免影響營業運作。這能幫助提高企業的利潤，因為如果現金轉換循環愈長，對債務的需求便會愈高，利息成本也會愈多。

The goal of the company is to shorten its cash conversion cycle as much as possible without hindering operation. This can improve the profits of the company because the longer the cash conversion cycle, the greater the need for external financing, since cash is not readily available, and such financing has a cost.

減短現金轉換循環的方法Methods for shortening the cash conversion cycle

  • 減短存貨階段：加快銷售出貨品
  • Reducing the inventory period by processing and selling goods more quickly
  • 減短收回應收帳款階段：加快收回應收帳款
  • Reducing the receivables collection period by speeding up collection
  • 加長支付應付帳款階段
  • Lengthening the payables repayment period by slowing down its payments

如果以上的行動不需要額外的成本，或負面影響銷貨，企業需要實行這些行動。

If the above actions do not require any additional costs or affect sales negatively, they should then be implemented by the company.

The margin note on the English handout marks these three moves as the management-efficiency ratios in 501: inventory, receivables and payables.

營業循環不要減應付Do not subtract payables from the operating cycle

營業循環只有存貨階段加收回應收帳款階段。減去支付應付帳款階段的，是現金轉換循環。

The operating cycle is only the inventory period plus the receivables collection period. The payables repayment period is subtracted in the cash conversion cycle.

加長付款會縮短現金轉換循環Lengthening payables shortens the cash conversion cycle

正確：拖慢付貨款，現金轉換循環變短。易錯：把三項都寫成「愈短愈好」。

Correct: slowing down payments shortens the cash conversion cycle. Trap: writing that all three periods should be shorter.

請茶的 45 日和 15 日Try Tea’s 45 days and 15 days

小麗父母的屯門請茶：存貨階段 25 日，收回應收帳款階段 20 日，支付應付帳款階段 30 日。營業循環 = 25 + 20 = 45 日。現金轉換循環 = 25 + 20 − 30 = 15 日。茶葉商若肯改成 40 日才收款，營業循環仍是 45 日，現金轉換循環變成 5 日。

Eslyn’s parents run Try Tea in Tuen Mun. Inventory period 25 days, receivables collection period 20 days, payables repayment period 30 days. Operating cycle = 25 + 20 = 45 days. Cash conversion cycle = 25 + 20 − 30 = 15 days. If the tea supplier waits 40 days, the operating cycle is still 45 days and the cash conversion cycle falls to 5 days.

教具：三個日數怎樣改變兩個循環Lab: how the three periods change the two cycles

小練習 505.2Quick check 505.2

題 1Q1

用請茶的 25 日、20 日、30 日，寫出兩個循環。

Use Try Tea’s 25, 20 and 30 days. State both cycles.

答案：營業循環 45 日；現金轉換循環 15 日

Answer: operating cycle 45 days; cash conversion cycle 15 days

題 2Q2

小美說：「加長支付應付帳款階段，現金轉換循環會加長。」對不對？

Karen says: “Lengthening the payables repayment period lengthens the cash conversion cycle.” Is she right?

答案：不對。加長支付階段會縮短現金轉換循環

Answer: No. Lengthening the payables period shortens the cash conversion cycle

2.1　現金管理Cash management

2.1.1　持有現金的成本和好處Costs and benefits of holding cash

持有現金的原因有兩項。

There are two reasons for holding cash.

進行交易For transactions

持有充足的現金以應付業務營運的需要。

Cash balances are necessary in business operations.

預防For precaution

企業需要持有充足的現金以應付突如其來的資金需要，例如火災、罷工、競爭者增加。

Firms need to hold some cash for unexpected future cash needs, such as emergencies like fires, strikes or competitors’ marketing campaigns, or unexpected future opportunities.

成本Cost

持有現金的成本：放棄利息收入。

The cost of holding cash: the interest income forgone.

好處Benefit

企業增持現金可提高其變現能力，出現現金短缺的風險便會減少。

Cash provides liquidity to the firm and lowers its risk of a cash shortfall.

2.1.2　現金管理的基本目的The basic goal of cash management

持有充足的現金以應付業務營運的需要，同時盡量減少閒置的現金，把持有現金的成本降至最低。

To maintain adequate cash for business operations and minimise the amount of idle cash so that the cost of holding cash is minimized.

2.1.3　支票延後Management of float

支票延後是付款人發出支票的時間，與收款人可以使用該筆款項的時間之間的差距。

Float is the gap between the day the cheque is issued and mailed and the day the funds are available to use.

出現支票延後主要是因為郵遞支票和銀行系統處理支票需時。Day 8 之後才可以使用該筆款項。The float runs from issuing and mailing the cheque to clearing. The funds are available to use after Day 8.

Undesirable consequences if a firm uses this technique to the extreme:

(1) the disbursement float turns out to be shorter than expected. (2) the cash is not received in time.

The cheque will be dishonoured. The firm’s reputation will be damaged. The firm’s credibility with banks and its relationship with suppliers will be damaged.

支票延後和現金管理Float management and cash management

  • 從付款人的角度看，延長支票支付延後對他們有利，因為他們可以延長持有該筆現金的時間。
  • From a payer’s viewpoint, it is preferable to lengthen the disbursement float.
  • 從收款人的角度看，縮短支票收帳延後對他們有利，因為他們可以盡快收取該筆現金。
  • From a recipient’s viewpoint, it is preferable to shorten the collection float.

企業可以透過縮短支票收帳延後的時間和延長支票支付延後的時間來增持現金。

By doing so, a firm can increase its cash on hand.

付款人延長的是支付延後，收款人縮短的是收帳延後。不要對調。

The payer lengthens the disbursement float. The recipient shortens the collection float. Do not swap them.

2.1.4　現金管理的基本原則Basic principles of cash management

原則 1：加快現金流入Principle 1: Accelerating cash inflows

目的：避免現金短缺，導致借取短期貸款及支付利息。

Purpose: to avoid a cash shortfall so as to avoid obtaining short-term loans and paying interest.

方法一：縮短支票收帳延後的時間。

Method (1): shorten the collection float.

  • 企業可以在主要的城市設立收帳中心，從而縮短郵遞時間。
  • By setting up payment collection centres in major cities, the time for mail delivery can be reduced.
  • 在銀行每天截數前存入支票，從而縮短交換支票手續所需（結算）的時間。
  • By depositing them before the daily cut-off time, the clearing time for cheques received can be shortened.

方法二：鼓勵現金付款。

Method (2): encouraging payments in cash.

  • 設立計劃去鼓勵顧客支付現金，而不是信用卡。
  • By implementing an incentive programme to encourage consumers to pay in cash instead of by credit card.
  • 例如：企業給予顧客會員卡，讓使用現金或八達通付款的顧客可獲取積分，換領禮品。
  • Example: issuing customers a membership card that allows them to accumulate points which can be redeemed for gifts.
  • 設立特快現金收銀處。

原則 2：延遲現金流出Principle 2: Delaying cash outflow

目的：企業盡量延遲支付現金，從而延長持有現金的時間。

Purpose: to slow down the disbursement process in order to keep the cash for a longer period.

方法：延長支票支付延後。

Method: lengthen the disbursement float.

  • 在偏遠的城市設立付款中心，從而延長郵遞時間。
  • By setting up a disbursement centre in a remote city, the mail delivery time can be lengthened.
  • 在星期五付款，令收款人不能在週末把支票存入銀行和過戶。
  • By making payments on Friday, the cheques are not deposited and cleared over the weekend.

原則 3：配合現金流入和現金流出的時間和金額（cash flow synchronization）Principle 3: Making sure cash inflows precede cash outflows (cash flow synchronization)

目的：有助企業避免支付額外的融資成本，以及降低持有現金的成本。

Purpose: to avoid having to pay extra finance costs, and it reduces the cost of holding cash.

方法：編製現金預算，調整現金流出，讓現有的現金餘額加上現金流入的總和足以應付現金流出（避免現金短缺）。

Method: match the timing and amount of cash inflows and outflows. By using cash budgeting to forecast the firm’s future cash flows, adjust cash outflows so that the existing cash balance plus cash inflows are sufficient to meet cash outflows (avoid a cash shortfall).

請茶的會員卡和星期五支票Try Tea’s card and Friday cheque

小麗在請茶櫃檯給現金或八達通的同學印會員積分，那是加快現金流入。茶葉商的支票放在星期五才寄，那是延遲現金流出。兩件事都要先看現金預算：餘額加即將收到的錢，夠不夠付這張支票。

Eslyn stamps membership points when a classmate pays Try Tea in cash. That accelerates cash inflow. The cheque to the tea supplier goes out on Friday. That delays cash outflow. Both still depend on the cash budget: existing cash plus money about to come in must cover that cheque.

小練習 505.3Quick check 505.3

題 1Q1

小明是付款人。他想多持有現金，應延長哪一種支票延後？

Bob is the payer. If he wants to keep the cash longer, which float should he lengthen?

答案：支票支付延後

Answer: the disbursement float

題 2Q2

請茶想盡快用到顧客的支票。應縮短哪一種？

Try Tea wants to use a customer’s cheque sooner. Which float should it shorten?

答案：支票收帳延後

Answer: the collection float

2.2　現金預算Cash budgeting

這一節不編製整份現金預算。要會的是定義、現金盈餘或短缺，以及它怎樣幫助現金管理。

This section does not ask you to draw up a full cash-budget worksheet. Learn the definition, the surplus or deficiency, and why the budget matters for cash management.

2.2.1　現金預算The cash budget

現金預算反映企業預測未來某段期間（例每年、每月）的現金流入、現金流出和現金餘額。

The cash budget shows the firm’s projected cash inflows and outflows over some specified period (on a monthly, weekly or even daily basis).

  • 期末現金餘額：企業預期在期末持有的現金餘額。
  • Ending cash balance: the amount of cash the firm expects to be holding at the end of the period.
  • 最低現金金額：企業希望持有的現金（進行交易／應付突如其來的需要）。
  • Minimum cash balance required: the amount of cash the firm desires to hold.

現金盈餘／短缺 = 期末現金餘額 − 最低現金金額

Cash surplus or deficiency = ending cash balance − minimum cash balance required

相差Difference 意思Meaning 行動Action
現金盈餘Cash surplus 正數Positive 企業預期持有的現金多於所需Hold more cash than required 把盈餘投資於短期投資以賺取回報（能簡單快捷地轉換為現金）The firm should invest the amount in short-term investment for a return
現金短缺Cash deficiency 負數Negative 企業預期持有的現金少於所需Hold less cash than required 進行短期融資（短期銀行貸款），令企業能持有不少於最低現金餘額的現金The firm should obtain additional short-term loans in order to meet the minimum cash balance required

正數是盈餘，去短期投資。負數是短缺，去短期貸款。不要看到「錢不夠」就寫長期借貸。

Positive means a surplus: short-term investment. Negative means a deficiency: a short-term loan. Do not answer with a long-term loan.

2.2.2　現金預算對現金管理的重要性The importance of cash budgeting to cash management

因為有現金預算：

With cash budgeting:

（1）預先計劃短期投資(1) Plan the short-term investment

企業能夠預測現金盈餘並計劃短期投資。因此企業能有多點時間分析不同的投資機會，並能作出更佳的決策。

A firm can plan in advance for short-term investment in the case of a cash surplus. This provides the firm with more time to analyse different investment opportunities and make better decisions.

（2）預先計劃短期貸款(2) Plan the short-term loan

企業能夠預測現金短缺並計劃短期貸款。因此企業能有多點時間尋找並分析不同的融資方法，並能作出更佳的決策。

A firm can plan in advance for short-term loans in the case of a cash deficiency. This gives the firm enough time to search for different financing options and negotiate a loan.

請茶月底的 $4,000Try Tea’s $4,000 at month end

請茶預期期末現金 $8,000，最低現金金額 $12,000。相差 = 8,000 − 12,000 = −4,000，是現金短缺。行動是短期銀行貸款，而不是把已經不夠的錢再拿去投資。

Try Tea expects an ending cash balance of $8,000. The minimum cash balance required is $12,000. Difference = 8,000 − 12,000 = −4,000, a cash deficiency. The action is a short-term bank loan, not an investment of cash the shop does not have.

小練習 505.4Quick check 505.4

題 1Q1

期末現金餘額 $20,000，最低現金金額 $12,000。相差是多少？叫甚麼？應做甚麼？

Ending cash balance $20,000. Minimum cash balance required $12,000. What is the difference, what is it called, and what should the firm do?

答案：+$8,000，現金盈餘，投資於短期投資

Answer: +$8,000, a cash surplus; invest in a short-term investment

題 2Q2

請茶的 −$4,000 應怎樣處理？

What should Try Tea do about the −$4,000?

答案：現金短缺，取得短期貸款以補回最低現金金額

Answer: cash deficiency; obtain a short-term loan to meet the minimum cash balance

3.1　應收帳款管理Accounts receivable management

應收帳款管理主要環繞企業如何制定應收帳款政策。

Accounts receivable management mainly concerns how accounts receivable policy is formulated.

3.1.1　應收帳款政策的三個要素Three elements of accounts receivable policy

1. 信用標準（Before credit period: To whom?）1. Credit standards (Before credit period: To whom?)

信用標準是指顧客要從企業獲得賒帳，須具備的最低信貸可靠性（或稱信用度）。

Credit standards refer to the minimum level of creditworthiness that a customer must have in order to obtain trade credit from a firm.

五個決定顧客信用度的因素（5Cs）：

Five factors determine a customer’s creditworthiness:

因素Factor 例子Example
品格 CharacterCharacter 有沒有責任感去支付債務whether the customer has a sense of responsibility to repay the debt
能力 CapacityCapacity 有沒有足夠的現金流量去償還債務whether the customer has sufficient cash flows to meet the obligation
資金 CapitalCapital 有沒有足夠的資金能夠支付債務whether the customer has sufficient capital to back up the debt
抵押品 CollateralCollateral 有沒有足夠的資產去保障貸款whether the customer has sufficient assets to secure the debt
狀況 ConditionsConditions 整體的經濟狀況industry outlook, general economic conditions

目的：防止有壞帳出現。

Purpose: to avoid bad debts.

2. 賒帳條款（During credit period: How?）2. Credit terms (During credit period: How?)

賒帳條款列明賒購貨品的還款條款。

A credit term states the repayment conditions for purchasing goods on credit.

  • 信用期限：債務人償還欠款的指定期限，又稱賒帳期間。
  • Credit period: the time period within which a debtor has to settle payment.
  • 現金折扣：債務人在現金折扣期限內還款所得到的折扣優惠。
  • Credit limit: the maximum amount that a debtor can obtain from the credit.
  • 現金折扣期限：債務人獲得現金折扣的還款期限。它較信用期限短，用來鼓勵顧客早日還款。

The English handout’s heading says three elements. Two are named: the credit period and the credit limit.

3. 收帳政策（After credit period: Overdue accounts?）3. Collection policy (After credit period: Overdue accounts?)

收帳政策列出一旦顧客逾期還款，企業應採取哪些行動來催收帳款，以免逾期應收帳款變成壞帳。

A collection policy is a set of guidelines covering actions for collecting overdue accounts receivable before they turn into bad debts.

  • 善意提醒
  • giving friendly reminders
  • 發出警告信或電郵
  • sending warning letters or emails
  • 造訪顧客辦公室
  • visiting the customer’s office
  • 僱用收帳公司
  • employing a collection agency
  • 對顧客採取法律訴訟
  • taking legal action against the customer
小新想賒一打珍珠Sam wants a dozen boxes of pearls on credit

小新想向請茶賒珍珠，下月才付。小麗先看信用標準：他上回拖了兩個月（品格），兼職收入不穩（能力）。這是賒帳之前、問「賒給誰」。信用期限和現金折扣是賒帳期間怎樣還。逾期之後的提醒和警告信才是收帳政策。

Sam wants Try Tea to let him take tapioca pearls now and pay next month. Eslyn starts with credit standards: he was two months late last time (character), and his part-time pay is uneven (capacity). That question is “to whom?”, before the credit period. The credit period and the credit limit are how the credit works during the period. Reminders and warning letters come after the account is overdue.

答案：品格

Answer: Character

Which C is “part-time cash flow is not enough to repay”? Which C is “no asset to secure the debt”?

答案：能力；抵押品

Answer: Capacity; Collateral

答案：短

Answer: credit limit

3.1.2　影響制定應收帳款政策的因素Factors affecting the formulation of accounts receivable policy

寬鬆Lenient 嚴謹Strict
因素Factors 低信用標準：盡量提供貿易賒帳給全部顧客
吸引的賒帳條款：(1) 給予顧客長的信用期限 (2) 增加給予顧客的現金折扣
寬鬆的收帳政策：一旦顧客逾期還款，延遲收帳行動 Low credit standards: provide credit to nearly all customers who request it
Attractive credit terms: (1) a long credit period (2) a large credit limit
Lenient collection policy: delay taking steps to collect overdue accounts 		高信用標準：訂定較嚴謹的信用標準，不提供賒帳給擁有欠佳還款記錄的顧客
嚴謹的賒帳條款：(1) 給予顧客短的信用期限 (2) 減少給予顧客的現金折扣
嚴謹的收帳政策：一旦顧客逾期還款，加快收帳行動 High credit standards: set stringent credit standards and credit limits to wipe out those customers with poor repayment records
Harsh credit terms: (1) a short credit period (2) a small credit limit
Strict collection policy: accelerate debt collection procedures
好處Benefits 吸引多點顧客，因此增加多點銷售Attract more customers so as to win more sales 維持較低成本Keep these costs at very low levels
代價Costs 1. 資金積壓在應收帳款上（可以用作投資）
2. 監督賒帳帳戶的成本提升
3. 收帳的成本上升
4. 較易出現壞帳 1. tie up capital (opportunity costs) that could otherwise be invested elsewhere
2. the costs of administering the accounts would rise
3. increased costs of collection
4. higher incidence of unpaid accounts (bad debts) 		減少銷貨，顧客更可能會光臨競爭者（較寬鬆的應收帳款政策）Loss of sales as customers turned to competitors whose policies were more lenient

改變應收帳款政策的影響如下。

The effects of changing the credit policy are as follows.

寬鬆的應收帳款政策Relaxing credit policy 嚴謹的應收帳款政策Tightening credit policy
降低信用標準Lowering credit standards 延長信用期限Lengthening the credit period, raising the credit limit 寬鬆的收帳政策Relaxing collection policy 提高信用標準Increasing credit standards 縮短信用期限Shortening the credit period, lowering the credit limit 嚴謹的收帳政策Tightening collection policy
銷貨Sales ↑ ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ↓
應收帳款Accounts receivable ↑ ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ↓
∵ 平均收帳時間 上升∵ average collection time rises ∵ 平均收帳時間 下降∵ average collection time falls
壞帳Bad debts ↑ ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ↓
∵ 平均收帳成本 上升∵ average collection cost rises ∵ 平均收帳成本 下降∵ average collection cost falls
變現能力Liquidity ↓ ↓ ↓ ↑ ↑ ↑
盈利能力Profitability 不確定Uncertain

銷貨和變現能力通常反向Sales and liquidity usually move in opposite directions

放寬：銷貨、應收帳款、壞帳上升，變現能力下降。收緊：三項下降，變現能力上升。

Relaxing: sales, accounts receivable and bad debts rise; liquidity falls. Tightening: those three fall; liquidity rises.

盈利能力寫不確定Profitability stays uncertain

正確：盈利能力不確定。易錯：看到銷貨上升就寫盈利一定上升。多了的銷貨要減壞帳和收帳成本，方向沒有註定。

Correct: profitability is uncertain. Trap: seeing higher sales and writing that profit must rise. Extra sales are offset by bad debts and collection costs, so the direction is not given.

請茶把信用期限加長Try Tea lengthens the credit period

小美說：「請茶把信用期限加長，銷貨和變現能力都會上升。」前半對，後半錯。銷貨上升，但平均收帳時間上升，應收帳款上升，變現能力下降。盈利能力仍然不確定。

Karen says: “If Try Tea lengthens the credit period, both sales and liquidity rise.” The first half is right. The second half is not. Sales rise, but the average collection time rises, accounts receivable rise, and liquidity falls. Profitability is still uncertain.

3.2　應付帳款管理Accounts payable management

  • 應付帳款管理是指企業如何制定應付帳款政策。
  • Accounts payable management mainly concerns how accounts payable policy is formulated.
  • 企業的應付帳款政策決定其賒購和償還應付帳款的程序。
  • A firm’s accounts payable policy governs the procedures for making credit purchases and repaying accounts payable.

目的：如果能夠好好善用應付帳款，這能減低對銀行貸款的需求，以及避免支付額外的借貸成本。

Purpose: an effective use of accounts payable can reduce the need to obtain bank loans and avoid paying extra finance costs.

決策：企業需要決定它應否 (1) 提早償還應付帳款以獲取現金折扣，或者 (2) 放棄現金折扣以持有更多現金。比較的是應付帳款和銀行貸款作為融資來源的成本。

Decision: a firm should decide whether it should (1) repay accounts payable early to take a cash discount, or (2) give up the cash discount. Compare the cost of using trade credit as a source of financing with that of using a bank loan.

獲取現金折扣Taking a cash discount 放棄現金折扣Not taking a cash discount
好處Benefit 減少其購貨成本Reduces its purchasing costs 可延長短期籌資，節省向銀行借款的利息成本The firm obtains short-term financing (the trade credit) for a longer period and saves on the interest costs
成本Cost 情況 1：沒有足夠的現金去償還應付帳款 → 可能要向銀行借款，這樣企業就得支付利息。
情況 2：有足夠的現金去償還應付帳款 → 承擔機會成本，因為企業須放棄運用這筆資金可賺取的投資回報。 Case 1: not enough cash to repay its accounts payable → need to obtain a short-term bank loan and pay interest.
Case 2: gets enough cash to repay its accounts payable → an opportunity cost is involved because it has to forgo the interest return from the money. 		承擔失去現金折扣的隱含成本The firm bears the implicit cost of losing the benefit of the cash discount

應付帳款政策的制定受到貸款利率和現金折扣的年率影響。

The formulation of an accounts payable policy is affected by the borrowing rate and the annual rate on the cash discount.

（1）貸款利率較高：放棄折扣(1) Borrowing rate higher: do not take the discount

如果貸款利率高於現金折扣的年率，企業便應放棄現金折扣。

If the borrowing rate is higher than the annual rate on the cash discount, the firm should not take the cash discount.

（2）貸款利率較低：獲取折扣(2) Borrowing rate lower: take the discount

如果貸款利率低於現金折扣的年率，企業便應獲取現金折扣。

If the borrowing rate is lower than the annual rate on the cash discount, the firm should take the cash discount.

筆記直接比較兩個已給的年率，不要求把「2/10、n/30」自行換算。利率高於折扣年率就不要為了折扣去借錢。

The notes compare two rates that are already given. You are not asked to turn “2/10, n/30” into an annual rate. If the borrowing rate is higher, do not borrow in order to take the discount.

茶葉商的折扣和銀行利息The tea supplier’s discount and the bank

茶葉商給請茶的現金折扣，年率是 36%。銀行貸款利率是 20%。20% 低於 36%，請茶應獲取現金折扣。若貸款利率改成 40%，40% 高於 36%，便應放棄折扣，不要借這筆錢去提早付款。

The tea supplier’s cash discount has an annual rate of 36%. The bank’s borrowing rate is 20%. 20% is lower than 36%, so Try Tea should take the cash discount. If the borrowing rate becomes 40%, 40% is higher than 36%, so Try Tea should not take the discount and should not borrow in order to pay early.

4　存貨管理Inventory management

4.1　存貨包括甚麼What inventory includes

存貨包括企業擁有的原料、半製成品及製成品。

Inventory includes raw materials, work in progress and finished goods held by firms.

為甚麼存貨可以高Why inventory may be kept high

能夠應付突然增加的需求。避免因缺貨（製成品不足）或生產停頓（原料不足）而損失生意。

It can meet unexpected increases in demand. Loss of sales due to stock depletion or production stoppages can be avoided.

過多存貨的成本Cost of excessive inventory

須承擔貯存成本及機會成本。資金用來購買存貨，就不能用於投資。持有過多存貨也會降低企業的變現能力。

Holding inventory involves storage costs and opportunity costs. The money tied up in inventory cannot be used for investment. Holding excessive inventory will even lower the firm’s liquidity.

4.2　存貨管理的目的Objectives of inventory management

存貨管理有兩大目的：保持充足的存貨（好處）；把與存貨相關的成本（貯存成本）降至最低（成本）。

Inventory management involves two main objectives: maintaining an adequate level of inventory (benefit); minimising the costs associated with inventory (cost).

4.3.1　經濟訂貨量（EOQ）Economic order quantity (EOQ)

4.3 是簡單控制存貨的技巧。這一節是經濟訂貨量，下一節是再訂購水平。

Section 4.3 is simple inventory control techniques. This part is the economic order quantity. The next part is the re-order point.

經濟訂貨量模型的目的，是找出把總存貨成本降至最低的最佳訂貨量。

The economic order quantity (EOQ) model aims at finding the optimal order quantity which minimises total inventory costs.

存貨循環Inventory cycle

虛線是平均存貨。每次訂得愈多，訂單次數愈少，平均存貨愈高。每次訂得愈少，訂單次數愈多，平均存貨愈低。The dashed line is average inventory. A larger quantity each time means fewer orders and a higher average inventory. A smaller quantity each time means more orders and a lower average inventory.

兩種存貨成本Two inventory costs

1. 訂購成本1. Ordering costs

訂購成本是向供應商訂貨所涉及的成本，包括下訂單和收貨等文書和行政工作所產生的金錢成本和時間成本。

Ordering costs are the money costs and time costs incurred from the clerical and administrative work involved in placing and receiving an order.

按每次訂貨（即每份訂單）計算。每次訂單訂購的數量愈多，需要的訂單愈少，每年總訂購成本愈少。

Ordering costs are normally expressed as a fixed amount per order. The higher the quantity ordered each time, the fewer the orders, and annual ordering costs will be lower.

總訂購成本與訂單數量成反比。

Total ordering cost is inversely related to order quantity.

2. 貯存成本2. Holding / carrying costs

貯存成本是持有存貨一段時間（通常為一年）所涉及的成本。

Carrying costs are costs related to holding inventory for a certain time period.

  • 貯存費
  • Storage and handling costs
  • 資金用來購買存貨的機會成本
  • Cost of capital tied up
  • 存貨損耗和產品過時所導致的損失
  • Loss due to depreciation and obsolescence
  • 保險費
  • Insurance costs

按每單位存貨計算。企業每次訂貨的數量越多，其平均存貨量便越多，全年的貯存成本也越高。

Carrying costs are normally measured per unit of inventory. The greater the quantity ordered each time, the more inventory the firm holds on average, and the annual carrying cost will be higher.

總貯存成本與訂貨量成正比。

Total carrying cost is positively related to order quantity.

當每次訂單的數量愈多（訂單次數愈少），貯存成本愈多，訂購成本愈少。

As the order size increases (order frequency decreases), inventory carrying cost increases while inventory ordering cost decreases.

兩句方向相反。訂得愈多，訂購成本下降，貯存成本上升。不要寫反。

The two costs move in opposite directions. A larger order cuts ordering cost and raises carrying cost. Do not swap them.

課本圖：P.162 Exhibit 5.1 Fig. 5.9（訂購成本）；P.163 Exhibit 5.2 Fig. 5.10（貯存成本）。課本練習：P.177 Q19a、b。

Textbook figures: P. 162 Exhibit 5.1 Fig. 5.9 (ordering costs); P. 163 Exhibit 5.2 Fig. 5.10 (carrying costs). Textbook exercise: P. 177 Q19a, b.

找出經濟訂貨量Finding the economic order quantity

在經濟訂貨量（總訂購成本等於總貯存成本時），總存貨成本達到最低水平。

At the EOQ, the total inventory cost (ordering cost and carrying cost) is minimal among all possible quantities.

總存貨成本 = 總訂購成本 + 總貯存成本

Total inventory costs = ordering costs + carrying costs

兩條成本線相交時，總存貨成本在正上方到達最低。那一點的訂貨量是 Q*。Total inventory cost is at its minimum directly above the point where the two cost curves intersect. That quantity is Q*.

根據上圖，當總訂購成本等於總貯存成本時，總存貨成本達到最低水平（兩條曲線的相交點）。因此 Q* 是經濟訂貨量。企業應該訂購 Q* 單位的存貨，把每年總存貨成本最小化。

Based on the graph, the total inventory cost is at a minimum when the total ordering cost and the total carrying cost are equal (the two curves intersect). Hence Q* is the economic order quantity. The company should order Q* units of inventory per order so as to minimize the total inventory cost per year.

公式Formulae

符號Symbol 意思Meaning
F 每次訂購成本（固定成本）Ordering cost per order
D 全年貨品需求量Annual demand for goods
C 每單位貯存成本Carrying cost per unit
Q 訂貨量Order quantity

總訂購成本 = F × D / Q

Total ordering cost = F × D / Q

總貯存成本 = C × Q / 2

Total carrying cost = C × Q / 2

總存貨成本 = F × D / Q + C × Q / 2

Total inventory cost = F × D / Q + C × Q / 2

EOQ = √(2DF / C)

EOQ = √(2DF / C)

請茶的紙杯Try Tea’s cups

請茶每年需要 1,800 箱紙杯。每次訂購成本 F = $100。每箱每年貯存成本 C = $4。EOQ = √(2 × 1,800 × 100 / 4) = √90,000 = 300 箱。在 Q = 300：總訂購成本 = 100 × 1,800 / 300 = $600；總貯存成本 = 4 × 300 / 2 = $600。兩項相等，總存貨成本 = $1,200。

Try Tea needs 1,800 boxes of cups a year. Ordering cost per order F = $100. Carrying cost per box per year C = $4. EOQ = √(2 × 1,800 × 100 / 4) = √90,000 = 300 boxes. At Q = 300: total ordering cost = 100 × 1,800 / 300 = $600; total carrying cost = 4 × 300 / 2 = $600. The two are equal, so total inventory cost = $1,200.

教具：經濟訂貨量Lab: economic order quantity

Use Try Tea’s F = $100, D = 1,800, C = $4. What is the EOQ? At that quantity, what is each cost?

總訂購成本Total ordering cost $600

如果每次改訂 600 箱，總存貨成本是多少？比經濟訂貨量高還是低？

If the order quantity becomes 600 boxes, what is the total inventory cost? Is it higher or lower than at the EOQ?

答案：訂購成本 $300，貯存成本 $1,200，總成本 $1,500，高於 $1,200

4.3.2　再訂購水平Re-order point

The English handout’s heading says “re-order level point”. The definition uses re-order point. They are the same level.

再訂購水平是企業須補充存貨的存貨水平。

The re-order point is the level of inventory at which a firm should replenish its inventory.

再訂購水平由三個因素決定：

The re-order point is determined by three factors:

  • 每日的存貨耗用量（或銷量）。需求突然變動會改變這項。
  • The daily usage (or sales) of inventory. Fluctuations in demand change this figure.
  • 供應商交貨所需的時間（即訂貨間隔期）。供應突然變動會改變這項。
  • The time it takes for the supplier to deliver inventory. Fluctuations in supply change this figure.
  • 用於應付突發情況的安全存貨水平。例子：銷量突然增加、供應商突然延遲交貨、生產突然停止（營運突然變動，例如罷工）。
  • The level of safety stock to cope with an unexpected situation, for example a sudden increase in sales, an unexpected delay of inventory delivery, or an unexpected production stoppage (fluctuations in operations, for example a labour strike).

再訂購水平 = (每日耗用量 × 交貨天數) + 安全存貨

Re-order point = (daily usage × number of days for delivery) + safety stock

存貨降到再訂購水平就落單。交貨之前存貨繼續下降，直到安全存貨附近；貨到才回升一個經濟訂貨量。The firm places the order when inventory hits the re-order point. Inventory keeps falling during delivery time, down towards safety stock. When the goods arrive, inventory jumps by one EOQ.

請茶的再訂購Try Tea places the next order

請茶每日用 8 箱杯。供應商需 4 日送到。安全存貨 20 箱。再訂購水平 = (8 × 4) + 20 = 52 箱。存貨降到 52 箱就落單，不是等到見底。

Try Tea uses 8 boxes a day. The supplier takes 4 days. Safety stock is 20 boxes. Re-order point = (8 × 4) + 20 = 52 boxes. The shop orders when inventory falls to 52 boxes, not when the shelf is empty.

SAO Limited　課本 p.168SAO Limited　Textbook p. 168

課本 Exhibit 5.4：SAO Limited 每日售出 10 單位。供應商需時 5 日交貨。安全存貨 40 單位。再訂購水平 = (10 × 5) + 40 = 90 單位。

Textbook Exhibit 5.4: SAO Limited sells 10 units of goods per day. The supplier takes five days to deliver the inventory to SAO Limited when it makes an order. If SAO Limited holds 40 units as safety stock, the re-order point is (10 units × 5) + 40 units = 90 units.

教具：再訂購水平Lab: re-order point

題 1Q1

請茶每日 8 箱、交貨 4 日、安全存貨 20 箱。再訂購水平是多少？

Try Tea uses 8 boxes a day, delivery takes 4 days, and safety stock is 20 boxes. What is the re-order point?

答案：(8 × 4) + 20 = 52 箱

Answer: (8 × 4) + 20 = 52 boxes

題 2Q2

SAO Limited 的再訂購水平是多少？

What is SAO Limited’s re-order point?

答案：(10 × 5) + 40 = 90 單位

Answer: (10 × 5) + 40 = 90 units
